name: Park Street and Camac Street
tagline: Kolkata's colonial-era dining and nightlife spine
description: A dense central grid of Art Deco blocks, old restaurants like Peter Cat and Trincas, bookshops and glass office towers on Camac Street. Serviced apartments and hotels sit above street level. Everything from the metro to coworking desks is within a short walk, which is rare in this city.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads who want to land, walk everywhere and not deal with commutes.
pros: Walk to cafes, bars and metro stations
Widest choice of restaurants in the city
Serviced apartments make short stays easy
cons: Heavy traffic noise and poor winter air quality
Pavements are crowded and often blocked

name: Salt Lake Sector V
tagline: The planned IT district east of the old city
description: Bidhannagar's tech quarter, laid out in wide blocks of software campuses, cafes and canteens. It is the one part of Kolkata built around office workers, so power backup and fibre are dependable. The area empties out at night, and most residents rent in the quieter numbered sectors nearby.
bestFor: Remote workers who prioritise reliable power, fibre and a coworking-heavy area.
pros: Most dependable internet and backup power
Wide clean roads, easy to cycle
Metro extension links it to the centre
cons: Dead and poorly lit after office hours
Long, slow rides to central Kolkata in rush hour

name: Ballygunge
tagline: Old-money South Kolkata streets and quiet lanes
description: A leafy residential belt of mid-century apartment blocks, tree-lined lanes and long-established Bengali families. Gariahat market sits at one edge for produce and cloth. Cafes, gyms and clinics are close by, and the metro line runs underneath, so it works well for a stay of several months.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting a settled, quiet local neighbourhood rather than a tourist strip.
pros: Good markets, clinics and gyms nearby
Direct metro access to the centre
cons: Landlords often want long leases and references
Water logging in lanes during monsoon

name: Bhowanipore
tagline: Dense, cheap and thoroughly local, just south of the centre
description: A crowded old neighbourhood of narrow streets, sweet shops, sari stores and small flats above ground-floor businesses. Rents are markedly lower than Park Street while still being a short metro hop away. It is the practical pick for anyone wanting a local base without paying central prices.
bestFor: Budget nomads happy to live like a resident and eat local every day.
pros: Rents well below the central average
Metro station and buses on the doorstep
Excellent cheap street food and markets
cons: Crowded and noisy through the day
Few flats have proper work desks or fibre

name: New Town Rajarhat
tagline: Kolkata's newest planned suburb of towers and malls
description: A grid of new high-rise condos, malls, an eco park and wide multi-lane roads northeast of the city. Flats here are modern, come with gyms and pools, and cost less per square foot than South Kolkata. The trade-off is distance and a car-dependent layout with little street life.
bestFor: Nomads travelling as a couple or family who want a modern flat with amenities.
pros: Modern flats with gyms, pools and backup power
Clean air relative to the old city
cons: Very car dependent, poor last-mile transport
Still half-built in places, feels empty
